::: {.lead}
In Lecture 5 you learned what an operating system does for a game: its
services, the scheduler and memory management. Today you see them on the
lab computer and on your phone. There are no new ideas: two short problems.
Do each one alone. The results of the activities are at the end of this
worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- The OS gives services to every app: processes, memory, files, devices and
  permissions.
- The **scheduler** shares the cores; the app on the screen gets the most
  time.
- When the RAM of a phone is full, the OS closes background apps, so a game
  saves its state.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right service.

::: {.match extra="the GPU"}
The game asks to use the microphone. Which service decides?
:   permissions

The game saves the progress to storage. Which service?
:   files

The game gets time on a CPU core. Which service?
:   processes
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · A tour of the PC: four tools of Windows

| Tool (shortcut) | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Settings › System › About (Win + I) | Windows version, CPU, RAM |
| Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) | processes, CPU %, memory |
| File Explorer (Win + E) | drives, free space, folders |
| Device Manager (right-click Start) | devices and their drivers |

A **device driver** is a small program that lets the OS control one kind of
hardware, such as a gamepad.

![The four tools of Windows.](images/pc-tour.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Four facts · 15 min"}
On the lab computer, write four facts, each with its tool:

1. the Windows version and the RAM;
2. the process that uses the most CPU now;
3. the free space of drive C:;
4. the graphics card (Device Manager › Display adapters).

*Your product:* four facts with the tool for each.

::: {.check}
A good answer: "Windows 11, 16 GB RAM (About); the browser uses the most CPU
(Task Manager); C: has 180 GB free (File Explorer); Intel UHD Graphics
(Device Manager › Display adapters)". Your values may differ, but each fact
must come from the right tool.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Which Windows tool?"}
Choose the right tool.

::: {.match extra="Settings › Battery|File Explorer"}
A game stutters. Which program uses most of the CPU now?
:   Task Manager

A new gamepad does nothing. Is its driver working?
:   Device Manager

How much RAM does the PC have?
:   Settings › About
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · A tour of the phone and the background

In a phone's Settings, **About phone** (iPhone: General › About) shows the
OS version, and **Apps › a game** shows its **permissions**. On a phone, a
game in the background is paused, and the OS may close it when the RAM is
full. On a PC, the game keeps running.

![Four places in a phone's Settings.](images/phone-tour.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/settings-explorer.html" poster="sims/settings-explorer.png" title="Settings Explorer: find the answer in a phone's Settings" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Two facts and one test · 15 min"}
1. On your phone (or first in **Settings Explorer**), write the OS version
   and the permissions of one game.
2. Start the game. Switch to another app for one minute, then go back.
   Did the game keep running, pause, or start again? Write why.

*Your product:* two facts and one sentence.

::: {.check}
A good answer: "Android 14 (About phone). The game: Microphone not allowed,
Notifications allowed. The game was paused. After a long time, or with many
apps open, it may start again, because the OS closed it to free RAM."
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Phone and background"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Display|the PC"}
Where does the phone show the Android or iOS version?
:   About phone

Voice chat in a game is silent. Where do you look?
:   Apps › the game › Permissions

Which OS pauses a game in the background?
:   the phone OS

Why may a phone close a game in the background?
:   its RAM is full
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. Which Windows tool shows the CPU % of each process?
2. What is a device driver?
3. Where does an Android phone show the permissions of a game?
4. What may a phone do with a game in the background when its RAM is full?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Task Manager.
2. A small program that lets the OS control one kind of hardware.
3. Settings › Apps › the game › Permissions.
4. Close it, so the game should save its state.
:::
